rules.rule: Check for urgent chest pain signs
Record known cardiovascular disease risk for chest pain
rules.problem: Invented management step: page only uses a known CVD risk > 20% as a risk factor.

rules.rule: Do an ECG for chest pain (doctor to review)
Check chest pain character for acute coronary syndrome
rules.problem: Omits 'Not relieved by rest or sublingual nitrates', 'Occurs more often than usual' and 'with minimal effort' from the page's feature box.

rules.rule: Check for tension pneumothorax or pneumonia in chest pain
rules.problem: No temperature check although pneumonia needs temp >= 38C; no oxygen saturation check.

rules.rule: Diagnose probable acute coronary syndrome in chest pain
rules.problem: Feature OR-group omits 'not relieved by rest/nitrates' and 'more often than usual'; 10 minute duration encoded as onset comparison with uncertain direction. Overall ECG/pleuritic/stable-angina structure matches the flowchart.

rules.rule: Diagnose probable stable angina in chest pain
rules.problem: Absence list is incomplete (missing nitrate-relief and frequency features), so stable angina can be diagnosed alongside features the page calls ACS. Duration uses <= at a boundary and doubtful direction.

rules.rule: Diagnose probable tension pneumothorax in chest pain
rules.problem: All of breathlessness, a sign and deviated trachea are required, stricter than the page's list of features; also requires pleuritic feature which is only the flowchart branch.

rules.rule: Diagnose probable pneumonia in chest pain
Urgent: chest pain with danger signs
rules.problem: 'Chest discomfort' new lacks the centre/left location; otherwise faithful. Page also has 'shock likely' (footnote 5) which is not encoded anywhere.

rules.rule: Urgent: probable acute coronary syndrome in chest pain
Urgent: chest pain worse on lying down, palpation or breathing deeply
rules.problem: Page only reaches this branch when ECG is normal/other/unavailable; rule ignores ECG (acceptable since ECG-abnormal goes to the urgent ACS box anyway).

summary: Most consequential: the ACS and stable angina rules omit two of the page's five 'is chest pain any of' features (not relieved by rest or nitrates; occurs more often than usual) and encode the 10 minute duration as an onset comparison whose direction is doubtful. The tension pneumothorax rule requires every feature, stricter than the page, and 'chest discomfort' and 'pallor of skin of face' do not match the page's location and generality. 'Shock likely' (footnote 5) and the temperature check for pneumonia are not encoded. Vital sign thresholds, danger signs, priorities and probable/possible labels are otherwise faithful.
